what_its_for: Regorafenib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of colorectal cancer (bowel cancer) that has spread to other parts of the body, a type of liver cancer called hepatocellular carcinoma, and a rare stomach or bowel tumor called gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST). It works by blocking signals that help cancer cells grow and by cutting off the blood supply that tumors need to survive.
how_to_take: Take regorafenib by mouth, once a day, at the same time each day. Always take it with a low-fat breakfast (for example, a small bowl of cereal with low-fat milk and fruit, or a piece of toast with jam — a meal with less than 30% fat). Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablets. Take it for 21 days in a row, then take 7 days off. This 28-day cycle is then repeated. Wash your hands before and after handling the tablets.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 160 mg (four 40 mg tablets) once daily for the first 21 days of each 28-day cycle. Your doctor may lower your dose to 120 mg or 80 mg if you have side effects. Never take more tablets than your doctor prescribes. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's exact instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it on the same day as soon as you remember, but only if it is still the same day. Do NOT take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. If a full day has passed, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time the following day. Call your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store regorafenib tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets inside the original bottle and tightly close the cap after each use. Do not remove the desiccant (the small packet inside the bottle that absorbs moisture). Throw away any unused tablets 7 weeks after first opening the bottle. Keep this medicine away from children and pets. Do not store it in the bathroom or near heat or moisture.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, pomelos, and Seville oranges (often found in some marmalades) while taking this medicine, as they can increase the amount of drug in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement), as it can make regorafenib less effective. Limit alcohol, as it may worsen liver problems. Avoid getting live vaccines (such as flu nasal spray or yellow fever vaccine) without talking to your doctor first. Tell your doctor about ALL prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, and herbal supplements before starting regorafenib, as many medicines can interact with it.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: severe stomach pain or vomiting blood or black tarry stools (signs of bleeding); chest pain, shortness of breath, or sudden numbness or weakness (possible heart or blood vessel problems); signs of liver problems such as yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe fatigue; severe skin reactions including blistering, peeling, painful redness, or sores in your mouth; signs of high blood pressure such as severe headache, blurred vision, or dizziness; fever, chills, or signs of infection; unusual bruising or bleeding; severe hand-foot skin reaction (painful blistering, swelling, or redness on palms or soles of feet); or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Regorafenib does not cure cancer, but it can slow cancer growth and help patients live longer. You may not feel any immediate change, as the medicine is working inside your body at a cellular level. Some patients may see results after a few treatment cycles. Your doctor will use blood tests, scans, and check-ups to monitor how well the medicine is working for you. It is important to keep all your appointments even if you feel well.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Regorafenib can be used in older adults, but side effects such as fatigue and weakness may be more noticeable. Your doctor will monitor you carefully. Liver problems: If you have moderate to severe liver disease, regorafenib may not be safe for you. Your doctor will check your liver function before and during treatment. Kidney problems: Dose adjustments are generally not needed for mild to moderate kidney problems, but your doctor will decide what is right for you. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT use regorafenib if you are pregnant, as it can seriously harm the unborn baby. Both men and women must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 2 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for 2 weeks after the last dose. Children: Regorafenib is not approved for use in children and teenagers under 18 years of age.
